review.reason: This preserved historical HuRI aggregate is retired because the current partner-scoped assertions for TTC19, DTX2 and CABP2 represent its evidence. review.summary: Retain demonstrated copper-binding capacity while leaving its physiological delivery role unresolved.
review.reason: The original positive abstract reports copper binding. The later human isoform-3 experiments measure 1:1 Cu(I) binding after deliberate CuSO4 loading with reduced glutathione and test competition under reducing conditions, with cysteine-mutant controls. PMID:31851937 finds no endogenous copper in purified E. coli-expressed COA6 and no COA6-associated copper peak in yeast mitochondria, but observes binding after CuSO4/glutathione reconstitution and questions its physiological relevance. Retain measured capacity as non-core, not an established autonomous copper-delivery role. The cellular C58S/C90S rescue defect is additionally confounded by cytosolic mislocalization.

review.summary: Retain the measured RNA-contact result as a non-core capability.
review.reason: The authentic supplementary row places C1orf31/COA6 in the mRNA-interactome set: detected in crosslinked and control samples, p.adj.DESeq=1 and p.adj.IC=0.00267341282992018. These are adjusted P values; the authors use either analysis at a 0.01 false-discovery threshold after UV crosslinking and stringent LiCl/LiDS oligo-dT purification. The nonsignificant DESeq arm therefore does not negate the qualifying ion-count arm. A mature soluble IMS protein has no established route to cytosolic poly(A) RNA in this experiment; the contacted RNA, cellular pool and tested product remain unresolved. That topology question does not by itself demonstrate nonspecific capture. Retain the HDA contact observation as non-core without an independently validated native RNA-processing function. The source-evidence index provides public original PDF/XLS URLs, hashes, the exact table row and assay/statistical locators.

review.summary: Refine the positive DTX2 pair to ubiquitin protein ligase binding.
review.reason: Three positive HuRI records map DTX2 to the canonical 622-residue product, with no reported truncation. Its official E3 ubiquitin-ligase identity matches GO:0031625. This verified partner class supports greater specificity than the TTC19 and CABP2 pairs, irrespective of their equal record counts. The assay does not establish a native COA6 ubiquitination pathway. The yeast assay does not reproduce mitochondrial IMS versus cytosolic/nuclear topology; that limits a native-contact interpretation but does not invalidate the reported positive pair or the independently established E3 partner class.
